subject: tall tower
title: The 5 Tallest Towers on Earth, Ranked (None of Them Is a Building)

scenes.text: The tallest towers on Earth aren't buildings. Nobody lives in any of them.
Number five: the Oriental Pearl Tower in Shanghai. 468 metres, finished in 1994.
scenes.label: Oriental Pearl · 468 m

scenes.text: Number four: Moscow's Ostankino Tower. 540 metres, and it was already standing in 1967.
scenes.label: Ostankino · 540 m

scenes.text: Number three: the CN Tower in Toronto. 553 metres, finished in 1976.
scenes.label: CN Tower · 553 m

scenes.text: Number two: the Canton Tower in Guangzhou, China. About 600 metres, finished in 2010.
scenes.label: Canton Tower · 600 m

scenes.text: Number one: Tokyo Skytree. 634 metres, opened in 2012. Almost two Eiffel Towers, stacked.
scenes.label: Tokyo Skytree · 634 m

description:
The five tallest free-standing towers on Earth, ranked by height. Skyscrapers and guyed masts don't count, so nobody lives in any of these.
Three of them are in Asia, and the oldest, Moscow's Ostankino, dates from 1967.
Which tower would you climb first?
first_comment: Which would you put at number one for the view, and what should we rank next?
